# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Reese Jennings**
[Street Address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross — Appeals Department
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 16, 2026**
- **Member:** Reese Jennings
- **Member ID:** W714739496
- **Reference number:** POC-0A9468429E-28212
- **Service denied:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
- **Requesting surgeon:** Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon), https://files.providernews.anthem.com/4827/pdf-Spine-Surgery-2024-10-20.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) that my surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented as medically necessary for me. The notice dated August 16, 2026 states that the records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking Anthem Blue Cross to reconsider that decision, because the records already in my file show a completed course of conservative care and imaging and exam findings that line up with the plan's own published criteria.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in my denial notice, which gives a date of **February 12, 2027**. I am sending this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

All quoted language below is from *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon), the policy identified above.

**1. Conservative management — the reason given for the denial.**

The policy states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

and

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

My records show both parts of that combination:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training, from April 1, 2026 through June 24, 2026 — 12 weeks, 18 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Complementary strategies (more than one):** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on May 16, 2026 that gave only about 2 weeks of partial relief.

That is physical therapy plus two additional conservative treatments, completed and documented, for this episode of care.

**2. The response to that care.**

The policy criteria include:

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My records describe 9 months of **progressive** neck pain that is not relieved by rest, NSAIDs that gave inadequate relief, and an injection whose benefit lasted about two weeks. My symptoms did not significantly improve after the completed course of conservative care.

**3. Duration of conservative care.**

The policy states:

> "Unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (physical therapy optional)"

My supervised physical therapy ran 12 weeks (April 1 to June 24, 2026), with medication management running alongside it over a six-month period. That exceeds the six-week period the policy itself names, and my radicular pain has continued.

**4. Imaging that correlates with my symptoms and exam.**

The policy states:

> "All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

and

> "When imaging studies demonstrate nerve root compression due to herniated disc or spondylotic osteophyte correlating with the distribution of signs and symptoms, and ANY of the following criteria apply:"

My MRI of the cervical spine dated July 22, 2026 shows a **C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression**. My symptoms match that level and side: radicular pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger, with weakness. My exam shows positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The MRI report itself is in my file; it was performed at [facility name] and read by [radiologist name, from the MRI report], and I ask that the radiologist's report be reviewed directly.

**5. Objective neurologic findings.**

The policy lists among its criteria:

> "Objective neurologic findings which correlate with a cervical nerve root impingement"

My chart documents a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and numbness and weakness in the right thumb and index finger — findings that correspond to the C6 nerve root compression seen on MRI.

**6. The policy's own waiver of the conservative-care prerequisite.**

I also want to point to this provision, because it speaks directly to the reason given for the denial:

> "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when myelopathy, weakness, or bladder disturbance is present."

My records document weakness in the right hand along with the MRI-confirmed C6 nerve root compression. I completed a full course of conservative care regardless — but under the plan's own language, a shortfall in conservative care would not be the correct basis for this denial where weakness is documented.

**7. Surgical risk factor addressed.**

The policy states:

> "Tobacco cessation. Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to spinal surgery is strongly recommended to reduce the risk of pseudoarthrosis."

I am a non-smoker. My records also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

## Two points where I am asking the plan to be specific

First, the policy defines a term this way:

> "significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs"

My records describe 9 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain, numbness and weakness in my right hand. My most recent recorded pain score is [pain rating from clinic note, if recorded], and the daily activities I cannot manage are [list of affected ADLs/IADLs from the clinic note or my own statement]. I am supplementing the file on this point rather than asking the reviewer to assume it.

Second, two of the provisions above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I was not able to obtain in full — including the components required under "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:" and the list of criteria that follows the nerve-root-compression provision. **If any specific item on those lists was the basis for this denial, I ask that Anthem identify it by name in the appeal response, along with the specific criterion the reviewer found unmet,** so that I and Dr. Duval can respond to it directly. The denial notice I received does not say which component was considered missing; it states only that an adequate trial of conservative treatment was not documented, and the records above address that point.

## What I am asking Anthem to do

I ask Anthem Blue Cross to overturn the denial dated August 16, 2026 (reference POC-0A9468429E-28212) and authorize CPT 22551 as requested by Dr. Duval. I also ask that:

1. The physical therapy discharge note dated through June 24, 2026, the medication and injection records, the MRI report of July 22, 2026, and Dr. Duval's operative plan be reviewed together as one record.
2. The review be conducted by a physician with training in spine surgery.
3. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I receive a written explanation that names the exact criterion from *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* that my records were found not to meet, along with a copy of the criteria used and information about my further appeal rights, including independent external review.

I have lived with this for nine months and have done everything that was asked of me before surgery was considered. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed. Thank you for taking a fresh look at the file.

Sincerely,

**Reese Jennings**
Member ID: W714739496
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated August 16, 2026 (ref. POC-0A9468429E-28212)
- Physical therapy discharge note (April 1 – June 24, 2026, 18 visits)
- Medication records and corticosteroid injection record dated May 16, 2026
- MRI cervical spine report dated July 22, 2026
- Office notes and letter of medical necessity from Duval, MD
- [Any additional records you wish to enclose]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
